content.user_title: Assess Data Quality with Six-Dimension Scoring
content.value_statement: Unclear data quality weakens asset, transaction, and governance decisions. This skill scores six dimensions, assigns grades, and recommends focused remediation.
actual_capabilities: Designs indicators for accuracy, consistency, completeness, conformity, timeliness, and accessibility.
Adapts dimension weights for general, data transaction, and accounting recognition scenarios.
Defines executable checks for formats, ranges, logic, relationships, and timeliness.
Calculates weighted scores and assigns A, B, C, or D quality grades.
Maps quality grades to reference valuation adjustment ranges with stated assumptions.
Produces assessment outlines, issue lists, remediation priorities, and monitoring plans.
limitations: It cannot inspect a dataset unless the user provides data, profiles, or test results.
Its valuation adjustment ranges are references, not licensed appraisal conclusions.
Industry-specific rules require domain definitions, regulatory context, and agreed thresholds.
Sampling conclusions depend on representative samples and documented confidence assumptions.

use_cases.title: Prepare data for accounting recognition
use_cases.description: Build a six-dimension assessment, document evidence, and identify quality gaps before data resource recognition.

use_cases.title: Support buyer due diligence
use_cases.description: Evaluate transaction data, explain its grade, and present reproducible checks for buyer review.

use_cases.title: Prioritize quality remediation
use_cases.description: Rank defects by severity and define focused actions for the weakest quality dimensions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic quality checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a six-dimension data quality checklist for [dataset]. State one measurable indicator and one evidence source for each dimension.

prompt_templates.title: Design a weighted scorecard
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GB/T 36344-2018 scorecard for [purpose]. Explain each weight, scoring rule, threshold, and required evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze assessment results
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess these quality results: [results]. Calculate dimension scores, the weighted total, the grade, major defects, and recommended remediation priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Develop an assessment and valuation package
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a complete assessment for [dataset and purpose]. Include scope, sampling, rules, scores, grade, delta range, caveats, remediation, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: Assess a customer dataset with 96% accuracy, 82% completeness, and delayed monthly updates.
output_examples.output: The assessment highlights strong accuracy, weak completeness, and material timeliness risk. It recommends filling critical fields and enforcing update deadlines before final grading.

output_examples.input: Explain whether a C-grade dataset should proceed to accounting recognition.
output_examples.output: A C grade indicates material quality gaps. Complete targeted remediation and reassessment before recognition, while documenting evidence, ownership, and remaining limitations.

output_examples.input: Create a report outline for transaction due diligence.
output: Weighted score, grade, and reference delta range

best_practices: Define the business purpose, dataset scope, evaluation date, and evidence requirements before scoring.
Use read-only access and avoid copying or retaining source data during assessment.
Document formulas, samples, thresholds, and exceptions so reviewers can reproduce every score.
anti_patterns: Do not raise scores to satisfy a preferred accounting, transaction, or valuation outcome.
Do not infer a final grade from undocumented samples or incomplete dimension results.
Do not present reference delta ranges as certified appraisal or regulatory conclusions.

faq.question: Which quality dimensions does this skill assess?
faq.answer: It assesses accuracy, consistency, completeness, conformity, timeliness, and accessibility.

faq.question: Can it score data for different business purposes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can adjust weights for general use, transactions, or accounting recognition when the user explains the purpose.

faq.question: Does it need the complete dataset?
faq.answer: No. It can work from representative samples or profiling results, but the assessment must disclose sampling limits.

faq.question: What does the A-D grade mean?
faq.answer: A indicates strong quality, while D indicates serious deficiencies. B and C represent increasing levels of remediation need.

faq.question: Can it provide a valuation coefficient?
faq.answer: It can suggest a reference delta range based on quality. A qualified professional must validate any formal appraisal conclusion.

faq.question: Can it replace a third-party quality review?
faq.answer: No. It supports assessment design and documentation, but independent review may be required for regulated or high-stakes decisions.
